newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN VW STAFF SAID TO END COURT ORDER WALKOUT.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN VW STAFF SAID TO END COURT ORDER WALKOUT.

text.p: Angry workers at the Volkswagen Brussels SA car assembly plant are expected to resume work later on Tuesday after a call by trade unions to end their spontaneous strike over a Belgian high court decision.

Personnel at the plant, a wholly-owned Belgian unit of German car maker Volkswagen AG (VW), walked out in disgust on Monday afternoon after the court decided to remove the magistrate leading enquiries into the country's child sex abuse and murder scandal from the case.
The court ruled the investigating judge had compromised himself because he had a free dish of pasta and a small gift from a group helping parents of missing children.
The wildcat strike at VW showed the depth of public feeling over the authorities' handling of the case.
The investigation has revealed police bungling and a shocking lack of coordination between various law and order forces, undermining public confidence in the justice system.

More than 500 VW workers demonstrated on Tuesday morning in front of the Brussels court building after the Monday night shift and Tuesday morning shift followed the example of the afternoon shift and also went on strike.
A joint statement by three trade unions said on Tuesday morning, "(The unions) urge all personnel to resume work at 1400 (1200 GMT)."
"(This means the afternoon shift) will go back to work," VW spokesman Marc Croonen told Reuters.
The unions called on workers to take part in a national public demonstration in favour of justice in the case on Sunday.
The VW plant has a total workforce of nearly 6,000 and assembles about 200,000 Golf and Passat cars per year.
